scope: For the actual periodic SU(2) Wilson coordinate laws with period n>1, two distinct neighbors (x,1) and (x,2) of target (x,0) each have every global LocalInfluence coefficient at least 1-K/beta. K is a constructed positive constant independent of n, volume and beta, obtained from the orientations of the actual staple fields 6 and 5+i. The proof uses a bounded continuous squared-distance separator and the exact tilted-Haar orientation second moment; no Gaussian approximation or supplied neighbor-influence estimate is assumed. The actual row is at least 2-2*K/beta, so beta>2*K excludes every global row budget at most one, including shrinking strict margins. Nonnegative weighting by numbers>=1 cannot restore contraction. This is a global raw-link comparison obstruction, not an obstruction to a physical mass gap or a gauge-invariant collective estimate. All twelve Clay obligations remain open.

squared_separator.definition: For distinct unit quaternions a,b, f(q)=|q-b|^2/(|q-a|^2+|q-b|^2). It is continuous, has values in [0,1], and has oscillation at most one.
squared_separator.pointwise_bound: The triangle inequality gives |a-b|^2<=2*(|q-a|^2+|q-b|^2). Hence 1-f(q)<=2*|q-a|^2/|a-b|^2 and f(q)<=2*|q-b|^2/|a-b|^2.
squared_separator.haar_input: For the actual tilt law with field A!=0 and beta>0, E|q-orientation(A)|^2=2*(1-axisMean(2*beta*|A|))<=3/(2*beta*|A|).
squared_separator.separation: For fields A,B with distinct orientations a,b, E_A f-E_B f >= 1-(3/|A|+3/|B|)/(beta*|a-b|^2). This improves the earlier unaudited distance-ratio proposal from inverse-square-root beta to inverse beta.

actual_wilson_geometry.target: (x,0), for any vertex x on every periodic lattice n>1.
actual_wilson_geometry.neighbors: (x,1) and (x,2) are proved distinct actual coordinates. Varying each aligned rotor separately changes only that exterior coordinate.
actual_wilson_geometry.baseline: Both rotor angles zero give actual target field A=6*1.
actual_wilson_geometry.changes: A pi/2 rotor in either of the two neighbors gives actual target field B=5*1+imaginaryUnit. The equalities concern the literal coordinateLaw, not a proxy conditional.
actual_wilson_geometry.orientations: A and B are proved nonzero and have different unit-quaternion orientations.

constant.property: K>0 is proved; K has no lattice-size, coupling or volume parameter.
constant.no_numerical_cutoff_claim: The formal threshold is the exact constant 2*K; a decimal approximation is not used in the proof.

influence_consequences.nonnegativity: The LocalInfluence predicate itself forces C(i,j)>=0: use equal configurations, the zero test, and oscillation budget one.
influence_consequences.individual: Each of C((x,0),(x,1)) and C((x,0),(x,2)) is at least 1-K/beta.
influence_consequences.row: The actual row is at least 2-2*K/beta. For beta>2*K it is strictly larger than one.
influence_consequences.trajectory: Along every diverging coupling sequence, including varying periods N_k>1, eventually no global LocalInfluence matrix can have all rows at most one.
influence_consequences.weighted: Weights at least one only increase the row, since nonnegativity is derived from admissibility.

scope_limits: The theorem concerns every global comparison in the raw one-link oscillation norm. It does not claim that the Wilson model fails to mix.

The rotated endpoint has nonzero plaquette energy. No estimate on its equilibrium probability is supplied or needed for the global supremum obstruction. Good-field restrictions require a separate argument.

The theorem does not analyze gauge quotients, gauge-fixed collective blocks or gauge-invariant observable propagation. Removing the prior flat gauge direction is not proved sufficient for contraction.
Neither the continuum limit, the original-transfer physical mass gap, nor a finite-energy continuum excitation follows.

existing_physical_dictionary.increments: WilsonTemporalInfluence.invariant_increment already identifies squared increments for gauge-invariant observables with those of the original full transition.

Do not assume that the small-mixed-budget theorem applies to the ground-row law: its ground-density factor still requires control.
